# WhitePact

> An independent pre-execution runtime authorization boundary for supported,
> configured AI agent actions. Authentication, intent and subscriptions alone
> do not authorize execution. Unsupported paths are not universally governed.

Operating doctrine: an agent may think and plan freely. Consequential actions routed through supported, configured WhitePact enforcement paths require independently evaluated authority. Direct calls outside those paths and compromised infrastructure are not universally controlled.

## Current public product

- [Product](__WHITEPACT_SITE_ORIGIN__/product): supported boundary and product scope.
- [Architecture](__WHITEPACT_SITE_ORIGIN__/architecture): conceptual control chain and limitations.
- [Developers](__WHITEPACT_SITE_ORIGIN__/developers): source references and integration entry.
- [Docs](__WHITEPACT_SITE_ORIGIN__/docs): local setup, API and MCP result handling.
- [Security](__WHITEPACT_SITE_ORIGIN__/security): threat boundary and disclosure.
- [Trust](__WHITEPACT_SITE_ORIGIN__/trust): implemented controls versus external assurance.
- [Enterprise](__WHITEPACT_SITE_ORIGIN__/enterprise): requirements-led evaluation.
- [Sovereign](__WHITEPACT_SITE_ORIGIN__/sovereign): authority analysis; not execution authority.
- [Repository](https://github.com/Guruprasath-Annadurai/Whitepact): implementation and release evidence.

## Boundaries

Implemented repository controls are not proof of deployed production behavior.
The conceptual chain does not claim every adapter invokes every subsystem.
Hash-chained evidence has documented verification boundaries; UNKNOWN external
outcomes remain uncertain and must not be retried automatically.
No SOC 2 or ISO 27001 certification or independent commercial penetration test
is claimed here. Hosted and commercial availability require separate verification.
Legacy scoring, leaderboard and incident routes are not the canonical product
entry points and their retirement requires explicit approval.
